title: shared_ptr and reference counting
concept: shared_ptr shares the same memory among multiple owners and is freed when the last owner disappears.

steps.title: Create shared_ptr
steps.explanation:
`make_shared<int>(100)` allocates an int and a reference counter together on the heap.

The current owner is one `a`, so `use_count() = 1`.

steps.title: Share — Increase reference count
steps.explanation:
With `shared_ptr<int> b = a`, `b` also becomes the owner of the same memory.

The reference count is increased to 2. Both `a` and `b` point to the same heap data.

steps.title: b goes out of scope — count decreases
steps.explanation:
At the end of block `{}`, `b` is destroyed. The reference count is reduced to 1.

Since the count is not 0, the heap memory has not been freed yet. `a` is still owned.

quiz.question: When is the memory of shared_ptr freed?
options: When the first shared_ptr is destroyed
When the last shared_ptr is destroyed and use_count becomes 0
quiz.explanation: shared_ptr automatically frees memory the moment its reference count becomes 0.

misconceptions.wrong: shared_ptr has no circular reference problem
misconceptions.correct: If shared_ptr references each other as A→B and B→A, the count will never become 0, resulting in a memory leak.
misconceptions.why: To fix this, you need to change one side to weak_ptr.

keyTakeaway: shared_ptr manages shared ownership through reference counting and is automatically released when the last owner disappears.
